unit.why: A short memorate, embedded in an ethical discourse on honouring Torah scholars: the author of Hokhmat Adam brings his book to R. Yosef Yozpa of Zolkiew, who warns that it will breed brazenness toward rabbis.
unit.boundary_note: the anecdote sits inside a homiletic discourse that begins in the previous division and continues into the next

stories.start_quote: ונהירנא כד הוינא טליא בא הגדול
stories.summary_en: The narrator recalls that as a child he saw the author of Hokhmat Adam show his book to R. Yosef Yozpa of Zolkiew before printing it; the rabbi praised it but warned that laymen reading the abridgement would think themselves halakhic authorities and grow brazen toward rabbis.

tags.why: The anecdote serves as an example inside an ethical discourse on honouring Torah scholars.

quotes: יסבור שהוא בעל הוראה כמו הרב
tags.why: Concerns halakhic authority and the effect of a halakhic digest on lay rulings.
The feared outcome is the arrogance of laymen toward rabbis.
It concerns the wisdom of non-Hasidic rabbinic authorities, though it does not much praise them.

missing_concepts: printing and approbation of a halakhic book
honour due to rabbis and Torah scholars (kevod ha-Torah)
danger of halakhic abridgements for laymen
